text:
sec-bot: automated scan (gitleaks) flagged a secret-like string in the CI artifact cache for repo `infra/telemetry-collector`. path: `runner-cache/gradle-cache/tokens.bin` :rotating_light:
alex: ugh. which token type? service account, api key? :eyes:
maria: looks like a long base64 blob, probably a service account key or old KMS-wrapped blob. can we confirm contents without leaking it further?
devops: i'm pulling the artifact into a safe env now, will inspect under restricted session. don't paste the secret here.
sec-bot: detection details: rule_id=gitleaks-aws-style, entropy=5.8, sample_snippet="***REDACTED***". artifact id: artifact-2026-03-19-1142, job: build-packages (self-hosted-runner-7).
john: i've started a quick containment plan: 1) revoke any matching key 2) rotate credentials 3) block runner network egress to remote endpoints if needed.
lia: @devops keep the runner online if possible to preserve logs, but switch it to isolated mode (no outbound creds).
devops: isolated mode on. I've copied the artifact to a secured bucket `sec-temp/1835123456` with access limited to sec-team and devops.
maria: next: search history + other repos. i'll run gitleaks + trufflehog across org and also check object storage for similar filenames.
sam: i'll run queries against cloud audit logs to see if that key was used: filter by serviceAccountKeyId and by caller IPs matching runner pool. sample query i'm running: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:service-account@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --limit 50`
john: we've prepared a revocation command. will run after we confirm mapping. e.g. `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable KEY_ID --iam-account=...` (we'll run it from sec bastion).
maria: found matches in two other artifact snapshots (artifact-2026-02-28-0901, artifact-2026-03-05-1630). no matches in git history so far (good sign), looks like it was injected by a job step that wrote creds into cache.
alex: any sign the key was used for exfil or prod access?
sam: checking logs now, earliest use seen 2026-03-01T02:12Z from runner-7 ip. actions include listBuckets and getObject on non-sensitive buckets. no write/delete on prod resources yet.
ciso: thanks for the quick triage. treat as P2 incident, notify customer ops if any customer data touched.
devops: rotating now: created new service account with limited scopes (artifact-read-only + logging-write). will update pipeline to use new short-lived key via OIDC flow. previous long-lived key will be revoked after rotation.
maria: action items for follow-up (post-incident):
- add artifact cache scrub step in CI (redact secrets before upload)
- enforce OIDC/Workload Identity for runners (no long-lived SA keys)
- enable artifact encryption-at-rest with KMS-managed keys
- increase audit log retention for artifact access to 1 year
- update RBAC: runners can't access service account creation/keys
- add a periodic gitleaks scan for artifact buckets
lia: i'll open a change ticket for RBAC + KMS integration and loop in platform security + devex.
john: please add a short blameless postmortem. timeline + root cause = job step leaked credential into cache. mitigation = rotate + CI change + RBAC + KMS.
alex: communicating to engineering org: recommended blurb: "We detected an exposed service credential in CI artifacts. The credential was rotated and access limited. We're rolling CI changes to prevent future exposures and increasing audit logging. No evidence of production compromise." can someone post to #incidents and #all-hands?
ciso: i'll prepare the incident advisory and coordinate with legal/comms. keep the channel updated.
maria: PRs opened: infra#442 (cache-scrub), ci#981 (enable-oidc), platform#128 (runner-rbac). linking them here for tracking.
sam: final note: we should integrate KMS envelope encryption when artifacts are uploaded so even if a blob leaks it's useless without KMS decrypt. i'll draft an implementation plan.
devops: rolling the CI patch to 4 runners now. monitoring for any pipeline failures. :white_check_mark:
sec-bot: incident status updated to "contained". ticket=SEC-2026-0319-17. next review in 48h post-rotation.
alex: thanks team. add learnings to the security runbook and mark follow-ups in the sprint. :thumbsup:
